title: Randolph County food delivery driver shares gas price problems: 'Working longer hours' - NewsBreak
text:
By Justin Lundy ,
1 hours ago
RANDOLPH COUNTY, NC. (WGHP) — The historic high gas prices mean more money out of your pocket.
In some way, we all rely on some mode of transportation every day, whether it’s to go to work, get home or, in some cases, have food and groceries delivered to our door.
Rising gas prices impact Greensboro food bank guests: ‘Takes your life dollars’ Depending on how much you drive or how many cars are in your household, that expense adds up really fast.
Triad Food Delivery Driver Speaks Out While juggling college classes and being a mother of two, Danielle Berry says she delivers food for Uber Eats and DoorDash.
Since the war with Iran began, she has noticed the price at the pump has only gone up.
“It definitely makes you think about the time you’re spending and how much you are making in that drive because it costs money to go from point A to point B to receive a profit in that,” Berry said.
Berry says that before the conflict in the Middle East, she was pretty relaxed when making deliveries. Now, that’s not the case.
“Definitely working longer hours. Longer sequences. Longer trips. Taking as many as you can. Not being as picky,” Berry said.
Berry says some delivery services are offering compensation.
“Uber Eats and DoorDash both have two separate gas-saving options right now that they use through their payment cards that you get paid from. Uber Eats has a certain amount of miles. They’ll add like $5 extra. But you’re talking 125 miles before you get that extra $5. And that’s a lot of miles to drive for an extra $5 with gas rising every single day,” Berry said.
Like many families trying to make ends meet, Berry says rising gas prices influenced changes to her budget.
“I downloaded different apps to track what I’m spending, how much I’m spending, where I’m spending it, to help me out with my budgeting skills,” Berry said.
